thread:
anna: Running a cross-region chaos sweep this afternoon. Goal: compare synthetic flood vs replay harness for failover paths and kernel-selection overhead when KV cache is cold vs warm. I sketched a small methodology, pinging folks who can help run and validate results. TL;DR: measure p50/p95/p99 tokens + kernel-switch delta + fallback model hit-rate.

mike: I can run the harness. Which config do we want for apples-to-apples? rps, seq lengths, mix?

anna: Good Q. Proposal:
- regions: us-east-1, eu-west-1 (two-region failover)
- sustained RPS: 400 per region, spike to 1200 for 30s every 5m
- trace types: synthetic (uniform short/chatty), replay (user sessions from last-week sample)
- seq lengths: 64/256/512 buckets (50/30/20)
- runs: cold-kv (new instance), warm-kv (prefill 10k prefixes)
- kernel variants: v2 (current), v2-quant-fix (candidate), compact-fallback toggle on/off

sara: Add: compare batching heuristics: continuous batching on vs off, and a lower threshold for batch aggregation (0.6->0.4). Those change token latency a lot under spikes.

mike: Command I'll use (local harness):
```
./bench/run --mode=chaos --regions=us-east-1,eu-west-1 --rps=400 --spike=1200 --seq-buckets=64,256,512 --replay-sample=last-week-10k --kernels=v2,v2-quant-fix --kv-warm=10k
```
I'll also push a variant that toggles continuous batching: `--batching=continuous|none`

jon: FYI previous dry run (non-chaos) showed a regression after the kernel picker change: seq512 p99 increased ~6% and we saw kernel-switch latency of ~1.1ms extra per token on fallback. Might be due to heuristics picking non-SIMD kernel for certain attention lengths.

perf-bot: Dry run summary (2027-08-19T14:22Z): p50=36ms p95=112ms p99=298ms fallback_rate=2.3% kernel_switch_avg=1.1ms error_rate=0.02% :bar_chart:

anna: Thanks. Can you dump the flamegraph/profiler for the kernel switch path? I want to see if we allocate or memcpy unexpectedly during selection.

sara: Attached quick profiler snippet from the regressed run:
```
# stack
kernel_selector::choose -> memcopy_if_needed -> quant_unpack -> cpu_conv
quant_unwrap: 0.45ms
memcopy_if_needed: 0.62ms
cpu_conv (seq512): 0.8ms
```
Looks like `memcopy_if_needed` spikes when sequence crosses 384->385 boundary. Maybe alignment heuristic bug.

mike: Good catch. I'll instrument the selector to log when we pick a non-SIMD path and correlate to seq len and batch size. Also will run with `--use-small-batches` to see behaviour at batch=1..4.

anna: For reporting, we need consistent metrics across harnesses. My suggestion: produce per-run CSV with columns: run_id, region_src, region_dst, rps, seq_bucket, kv_state, kernel_variant, batching_mode, p50_ms, p95_ms, p99_ms, fallback_pct, kernel_switch_ms_avg, error_pct. Then we can aggregate and plot delta between synthetic vs replay.

jon: Agreed. Also capture arrival shape histograms (inter-arrival timings) from replay vs synthetic so we can show they’re comparable. Replay tends to have more burstiness -> more batch coalescing, which masks some kernel costs.

perf-bot: New run completed (1923456742): run_id=run-1923456742, p50=42ms, p95=130ms, p99=360ms, fallback_pct=3.1%, kernel_switch_avg=1.5ms :warning:

mike: Noted the p99 climb on replay harness compared to synthetic. Replays show higher fallback_pct. I'll attach logs.

anna: Let's triage sources: 1) selector boundary bug at 385 2) batching thresholds causing odd batch sizes 3) KV cache priming variance between regions (latency to fetch prefixes on miss). Prioritize selector fix first.

sara: Quick mitigation: we can add a tiny hysteresis in selector: prefer SIMD kernel up to 410 unless mem footprint estimate > threshold. Should reduce switch noise. I'll open PR.

deploy-bot: deploy request: PR #4587 opened by sara -> runtime/kernel-selector: add-simd-hysteresis. CI: passed, staging: queued.

anna: Great. Once PR lands, let's re-run the chaos sweep with identical seeds. Need CC: @sara @mike @jon. After that we'll run the apple-to-apples report and doc results in the perf-board.

mike: I can re-run tonight and produce the CSVs. Will also attach raw kv-miss traces per region.

jon: One more ask: include model-variant fallback counts (quant vs fp) as that's a contributor to per-token latency.

anna: Yep. Add model_variant column. Thanks everyone. If the PR reduces kernel_switch_avg by >0.6ms and fallback_pct stays <=1%, we can mark regression mitigated.

sara: Will follow up with PR link and quick before/after flamegraphs.

perf-bot: follow-up note: schedule run for 1923459000 (overnight) queued. :white_check_mark:

anna: Perfect. I'll capture the final CSVs and schedule a short sync tomorrow to agree on rollout for the selector tweak. :thumbsup:
